==English==
{{wp}}
{{commonscat|Placards}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{sense|plate}} {{alter|en|plackart|plaquet}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|placard||official document}}, from {{der|en|frm|placard}}, {{m|frm|placart}}, {{m|frm|plaquart||a placard, a writing pasted on a wall}}, from the {{der|en|fro|-}} verb {{m|fro|plaquer}}, {{m|fro|plaquier||to stick or paste, roughcast}}, from {{der|en|dum|placken}}, {{m|dum|plecken||to glue or fasten, plaster, patch}}, ultimately from {{der|en|gem-pro|*plaggą||a piece of cloth, patch}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|plaque|ard}}.

Related to {{cog|gml|placken||to smear with lime or clay, plaster}}, {{cog|stq|Plak}}, {{m|stq|Plakke||a hit, smack, slap}}, {{cog|de|Placken||a spot, patch}}, {{cog|is|plagg||a document}}, {{cog|he|פלקט|tr=plakat|t=a large sheet of paper, typically with a photo or writing, posted on the wall}}, {{cog|en|play}}. Compare also Modern {{cog|nl|plakkaat||placard}}, {{cog|stq|Plakoat||a placard, poster}}. More at {{l|en|play}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈplæk.ɑːd/|a=UK}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-placard.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈplæk.ɑɹd/|a=US}}, {{IPAchar|/ˈplæk.ɚd/}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[sheet]] of [[paper]] or [[cardboard]] with a written or printed [[announcement]] on one side for [[display]] in a [[public]] place.
#* {{RQ:Eliot Middlemarch|passage=Especially from Mr. Borthrop Trumbull, a distinguished bachelor and auctioneer of those parts, much concerned in the sale of land and cattle: a public character, indeed, whose name was seen on widely distributed '''placards''', and who might reasonably be sorry for those who did not know of him.}}
#* {{RQ:Sinclair Jungle|chapter=4|passage=He brought out the '''placard''', which was quite a work of art. It was nearly two feet long, printed on calendered paper, with a selection of colors so bright that they shone even in the moonlight.}}
#* {{RQ:Woolf Voyage Out|passage=While her husband read the '''placards''' pasted on the brick announcing the hours at which certain ships would sail for Scotland, Mrs. Ambrose did her best to find information.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=2024-08-01|author=Josh Halliday, Neha Gohil|title=Police in England urged to protect mosques as far right plans more rallies|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/article/2024/aug/01/police-in-england-urged-to-protect-mosques-as-far-right-plans-more-rallies|text=In Manchester and in Aldershot in Hampshire, asylum seeker accommodation was targeted by demonstrators carrying '''placards''' that read “deport them, don’t support them” and “no apartments for illegals”.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240824100854/https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/article/2024/aug/01/police-in-england-urged-to-protect-mosques-as-far-right-plans-more-rallies}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[public]] [[proclamation]]; a [[manifesto]] or [[edict]] issued by [[authority]].
#* {{RQ:Howell Epistolae|1 May 1632|A Survey of the Seventeen Provinces|passage=All '''placards''' or edicts are published in his name.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Permission given by authority; a license.
#: {{ux|en|to give a '''placard''' to do something}}
# {{lb|en|historical}} An extra [[plate]] on the lower part of the [[breastplate]] or [[backplate]] of [[armour]].
# {{lb|en|historical}} A kind of [[stomacher]], often adorned with jewels, worn in the fifteenth century and later.
# The [[woodwork]] and [[frame]] of the [[door]] of a [[closet]] etc.

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# To [[affix]] a placard to, or mark with a placard nearby.
#* {{RQ:Twain Tramp Abroad|page=108|passage=The inner walls of the church were '''placarded''' with large mural tablets of copper, bearing engraved inscriptions celebrating the merits of old Heilbronn worthies of two or three centuries ago, {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Bramah Max Carrados Mysteries|passage={{...}} we have railed off the part and '''placarded''' it "Dangerous" {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Hardy Jude the Obscure|chapter=VIII|passage=In the afternoon Sue and the other people bustling about Kennetbridge fair could hear singing inside the '''placarded''' hoarding farther down the street.}}
# To [[announce]] with placards.
#: {{ux|en|to '''placard''' a sale}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1871|title=Paris under the Commune|author={{w|John Leighton (artist)|John Leighton}}|url=https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/10861/pg10861-images.html|passage=These men, who have already caused you so much harm, whom you yourselves dispersed on the 31st of October, are '''placarding''' their intention to protect you against the Prussians, who have only made an appearance within our walls, {{...}}}}
